query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount (1–3 atomic percent) of yttrium (Y) to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures without significantly degrading its mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–3 atomic percent yttrium (Y) into the alloy composition.
generation.conditions: High-temperature exposure at 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere for up to 100 hours, under tensile loading at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable yttrium oxide (Y2O3) layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Yttrium has a strong affinity for oxygen and forms a dense, stable oxide (Y2O3) that acts as a protective barrier, reducing oxygen ingress into the alloy and mitigating oxidation-related degradation.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy will exhibit significantly reduced oxidation rates (e.g., a reduction by at least 50% in mass gain due to oxidation) compared to untreated HfNbTaTiZr, while maintaining room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16% and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, which has poor oxygen resistance at high temperatures, leading to rapid oxidation and degradation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is valid for temperatures up to 1000 °C, oxygen-containing atmospheres, and exposure times up to 100 hours. Mechanical performance should remain within the specified ranges of ductility and yield strength.
generation.uncertainty: The exact impact of yttrium addition on the alloy's mechanical properties and the long-term stability of the Y2O3 layer under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: untreated HfNbTaTiZr and HfNbTaTiZr with 1–3 atomic percent yttrium. Expose both sets to 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere for 100 hours. Measure oxidation rates (mass gain) and mechanical properties (tensile ductility and yield strength) before and after exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yttrium-modified alloy does not show at least a 50% reduction in oxidation rate compared to the untreated alloy or if its mechanical properties fall outside the specified ranges, the hypothesis will be falsified.
